findings.title: Date overrides bypass busy-time checks
findings.body: When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before checking `busy`. Date overrides add availability; they do not make existing bookings or calendar events disappear. A fixed host can therefore be shown as available during an existing booking or busy calendar event, allowing a conflicting round-robin booking.

findings.title: Working-hours validation can accept unavailable slots and reject valid ones
findings.body: This only returns a match when a same-day interval fails the bounds check. If the host has no interval for that weekday, `.find` returns nothing and the slot is accepted; if the host has multiple intervals that day, a slot inside one can be rejected because it falls outside another. It also compares only the slot start time, so an event can extend past the host’s availability end. In round-robin availability assembled from other hosts, this can expose slots the fixed host cannot take.

findings.title: Zero-length date overrides are never recognized as equal
findings.body: This compares two Dayjs objects with `===`, which tests object identity rather than whether their timestamps match. For a zero-length override, the intended equality case is skipped; the subsequent range checks can then incorrectly allow a slot that spans that timestamp instead of treating the override as unavailable.
